items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to emissions
of toxic air contaminants; and to amend the state finance law, in relation to
establishing the community benefit fund
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4371

SPONSOR: BIAGGI
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to emis-
sions of toxic air contaminants; and to amend the state finance law, in
relation to establishing the community benefit fund

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To establish standards for and limits on the emissions of toxic air
contaminants, and to create a mechanism to enforce such limits via civil
and administrative penalties.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the Environmental Conservation law by adding a new
section 19-0329.

Section 1 subdivision 1 defines the following. terms: "adjacent to",
"economically distressed area", "ethnic group", "environmental justice
community", "fenceline", "major source", "minority community", and
"toxic air contaminant".

Section 1 subdivision 2 requires the Department of Environmental Conser-
vation to promulgate standards for toxic air contaminants including
benzene, formaldehyde, vinyl chloride, polychlorinated dibenzodioxins,
polychlorinated dibenzofurans, trichloroethylene and mercury.

Section 1 subdivision 3 requires large air contamination sources located
near economically distressed or minority communities to install and
operate monitoring systems which measure the concentration levels of
these contaminants. It also requires owners of large air contamination
sources to submit publicly-accessible quarterly reports to the Depart-
ment of Environmental Conservation containing the results acquired by
these monitoring systems.

Section 1 subdivision 4 prohibits violation of the Department of Envi-
ronmental Conservation's standards, and permits the withholding of
permits or approvals based upon such violations.

Section 1 subdivision 5 permits both civil and administrative sanctions
as penalty for failure to comply with the requirements of this section.
Sanctions collected from major contamination sources for violation of
these air quality standards will be paid into a community benefit fund,
which will be used to implement environmental benefit projects in
economically distressed or minority communities located near such large
air contamination sources.

Section 2 amends the Finance law by adding a new section 97-ccc. This
section establishes a community benefit fund to be held in the custody
of the comptroller, the commissioner of taxation and finance,e and, he
commissioner of environmental conservation. The money in this fund may
net be distributed except upon completion of a voucher by the commis-
sioner of environmental conservation.

Section 3 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This legislation is necessary to reduce emissions of toxic air contam-
inants in New York State, and lessen their impact in low income and
communities of color.

In the United States, low income communities and communities of color
are the socioeconomic groups most likely to inhale harmful air pollu-
tants.(1) While Caucasion people inhale 17* less air pollution than is
caused by their consumption of goods and services, African American and
Hispanics inhale an average of 56* and 63* more air pollution than is
caused by their consumption of goods and services.(2) Inhalation of
harmful air pollutants increases the risk of heart disease, cerebrovas-
cular disease, lower respiratory infection, lung cancer, and chronic
obstructive pulmonary disease while concurrently reducing life expectan-
cy.(3)

This inequity is illustrated by the dense concentration of industrial
facilities and highways located in the Bronx.(4) Such facilities produce
high levels of toxic air pollutants in the borough with the highest
poverty rate and highest minority-residency rate.(5) correspondence with
these high rates of toxic air pollutants, marginalized residents of the
Bronx are hospitalized for asthma, respiratory illness, and cardiovascu-
lar disease at a much higher rate than white residents in other sections
of the City.(6) This inequitable pollution pattern is replicated in
communities of color across New York State, including: Buffalo, Albany,
Rochester and Syracuse.(7) This legislation preserves and protects the
quality of air in New York State by limiting the emissions of toxic air
pollutants including benzene, formaldehyde, vinyl chloride, polychlori-
nated dibenzodioxins, polychlorinated dibenzofurans, trichloroethylene
and mercury through standards set by the Department of Environmental
Conservation. This legislation also provides a means for redressing the
disproportionate harm caused by toxic air pollutants to economically
distressed and racial-ethnic minority communities in its creation of a
community benefit fund. This fund will be financed by fees paid by
violators of the emission standards created herein, and will be applied
to the implementation of environmental projects to benefit affected
communities.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.
1 "Harmful air pollutants" in this context refers to Particulate Matter
("PM") particles which are 2.5 micrometers or less in diameter and can
thus be inhaled into the lungs. Environmental Protection Agency, "Parti-
culate Matter (PM2.5) Trends", ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY, last
updated June 8, 2020, available at
https://www.epaqov/air-trends/particulate-matter-pm25-trends; Brandt,
Beck & Mersha, Air pollution, racial disparities, and COVID-19 mortal-
ity, 146 J. ALLERGY & CLINICAL IMMUNOLOGY 61, 61 (2020); see also
Tessum, et al, Inequity in consumption of goods and services adds to
racial-ethnic disparities in air pollution exposure, 116 P.N.A.C. 6001,
6001 (2019).
2 Tessum, et al., supra note 1 at 6001; see also Hazar Kilani, "'Asthma
alley': why minorities bear burden of pollution inequity caused by white
people", The Guardian, April 4, 2019.
3 Cohen, et al., Estimates and 25-year trends of the _global burden of
disease attributable to ambient air pollution: an analysis of data from
the Global Burden of Diseases Study 2015, 389 LANCET 1907, 1907, 1909
(2017).
4 Namratha Somayajula, "Air Pollution in US Exacerbates Covid-19
Dangers", HUMAN RIGHTS WATCH, April 20, 2020.
5 Union of Concerned Scientists, Inequitable Exposure to Air Pollution
from Vehicles in New York State, UNION OF CONCERNED SCIENTISTS USA
(2019).
6 New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, Air Pollution
and the Health of New Yorkers: The Impact of Fine Particles and Ozone,
PLAN NYC.
7 Union of Concerned Scientists, supra note 5 at figure 1.  NEW YORK
STATE ASSEMBLY MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF LEGISLATION submitted in accord-
ance with Assembly Rule III, Sec 1(f)

summary: Directs the department of environmental conservation to promulgate air quality standards for emissions of certain toxic air contaminants.
title: Relates to emissions of toxic air contaminants

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 96
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 4371-D, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
      emissions of toxic air contaminants"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would require the Department of  Environmental  Conservation
(DEC) to promulgate air quality standards for toxic air contaminants and
establish standards on fenceline monitoring for major sources.
 
  Major sources of the toxic air contaminants identified in the bill are
regulated  by  National  Emission Standards for Hazardous Air Pollutants
and DEC regulations, which provide the regulatory language for DEC staff
to enforce specific emission restrictions from process emission  sources
for  criteria  and  non-criteria  air  contaminants. Part 212 is used in
conjunction with other state and federal regulations to control criteria
air contaminants and non-criteria air contaminants, as well as toxic air
contaminants. Additionally, existing DEC guidance specifies  annual  and
short-term  ambient  guideline  concentrations for the toxic air contam-
inants referenced in this bill, and DEC has incorporated  toxic  contam-
inants,  emission  limits,  and emission control requirements into major
source permits since the inception of the Title V program.    These  DEC
guidance  documents  also  consider off-site fenceline concentrations in
relation to the annual and short-term guideline concentrations.
 
  Currently, DEC is undertaking a statewide community air quality  moni-
toring effort in ten disadvantaged communities that are home to an esti-
mated five million New Yorkers. This effort will help DEC target strate-
gies to reduce air pollution in these burdened areas to help achieve the
goals of the State's Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act.
 
  Through  its  existing  authority  and  regulatory  programs,  DEC has
already put in place strong protections against toxic air  contaminants.
As a result of these programs, there are very few remaining major sourc-
es  of toxic air contaminants of the sorts defined in this bill. Requir-
ing DEC to promulgate air quality standards and develop regulations  for
monitoring  plans for fenceline systems that are already overseen by DEC
under existing regulatory  authority  is  duplicative,  unnecessary  and
could divert state resources from implementing other crucial programs to
protect New Yorkers.
 
  Therefore, I am constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
